question: Shared. Both meta-analyses estimate how much aerobic exercise, against non-exercise control, improves cognition in older adults with MCI, measured with cognitive tests (clinical/cognitive channel). The differences are allowed and recorded as candidate explanations. P-680 pools a per-study composite of all cognitive domains, and P-683 the global-cognition domain. P-680's 'aerobic' stratum includes a music-accompanied stepping trial and an aerobic-dance trial, which P-683 assigns to its music and dance nodes. P-680 left amnestic-labelled trials out of its analysis, while P-683 includes them. P-680 admits non-randomised controlled studies, and P-683 only RCTs.
metric: Standardised mean difference of pre-post change scores with standardised mean difference of change scores (match). P-680 uses CMA's standard difference in means standardised by change-score SD; P-683 uses Hedges' g of change scores (change SD imputed with r = 0.68 where missing).

figures.P-680: Aerobic exercise vs control (5 studies, 6 comparisons, df = 5): SMD 1.442, 95% CI 0.624-2.260 (abstract and Discussion; the Results print 0.642-2.260). The Z of 3.456 gives SE = 1.442/3.456 = 0.417 and CI 1.442 +/- 1.96*0.417 = 0.624-2.260, so 0.624 is the consistent bound. I2 = 88.9%, prediction interval -1.440 to 4.324. All exercise: 1.165 (0.741-1.589).
figures.P-683: Aerobic exercise without music vs control, global cognition (k = 26 effect sizes, 11 trials, n = 683): g = 0.48 (95% CI 0.18-0.79), SE about (0.79-0.18)/3.92 = 0.156. Excluding high risk-of-bias studies: 0.6 (0.28-0.93). Aerobic with music: 1.2 (0.47-1.94). Dance: 0.55 (0.13-0.96). Music-supported exercise (AEwM + dance): 0.7 (0.33-1.08). All three exercise types together, multivariate model at rho = 0.6: 0.53 (0.16-0.90).

matched_figure_check: No figure in either paper is reported under the other's full condition. P-683 never pools an 'aerobic' class that includes music and dance trials on a composite outcome, and P-680 reports no global-cognition-only or music-free aerobic estimate. The nearest partial matches do not reconcile the pair. (a) Study quality: P-680 excluded poor-quality studies, and P-683's AEwtM estimate without high risk-of-bias studies is 0.6 (0.28-0.93). P-680's 1.442 lies outside that interval, and 0.6 lies below P-680's lower bound of 0.624, by 0.024 only. The two-sample z is (1.442-0.6)/sqrt(0.417^2+0.166^2) = 1.88. (b) All exercise types pooled: P-683's multivariate 0.53 (0.16-0.90) against P-680's all-exercise 1.165 (0.741-1.589); each lies outside the other's interval. P-680's pool also contains resistance and multimodal trials, which P-683 excludes. The gap survives the partial matches, narrowly on the quality-matched figure.
performance_validity: Not a performance comparison (intervention effect sizes); condition 5 does not apply.

candidate_explanations.difference: Intervention classification. P-680's aerobic stratum includes Song & Yu 2019 (stepping exercise, which P-683 classes as aerobic with music) and Qi 2019 (which P-683 classes as dance, as Qi et al. 2018, the same article, DOI 10.3892/etm.2018.7006). P-683 finds music-accompanied aerobic exercise has a larger effect (g = 1.2).
candidate_explanations.quote: aerobic exercise showed a large effect on cognition (Amjad et al., 2019; Bademli et al., 2019; Qi et al., 2019; Song & Yu, 2019; Varela et al., 2012)

candidate_explanations.difference: Intervention classification (P-683 side): Song & Yu 2019 is an AEwM trial, not AEwtM.
candidate_explanations.quote: Four trials investigated the effects of AEwM (Choi & Lee, 2018; Nagamatsu et al., 2012; Shimizu et al., 2018; Song & Yu, 2019)

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome construct. P-680 pools one composite of all cognitive tests per study, while P-683 pools the global-cognition domain (screening instruments) only. P-683's own AEwtM effects on other domains are smaller (e.g. executive function 0.05), so this difference may not run in the direction that would explain P-680's larger value.
candidate_explanations.quote: we performed the meta-analysis of cognition with composite cognitive scores which combined scores from all cognitive domains

candidate_explanations.difference: Population. P-680 left amnestic MCI out of its quantitative analysis, while P-683's AEwtM node includes amnestic trials (e.g. Tarumi 2019, Stuckenschneider 2021).
candidate_explanations.quote: The amnestic MCI population was not included in our quantitative analysis due to insufficient data.

candidate_explanations.difference: Study design. P-680 admits any controlled design, rating quality with a checklist for randomised and non-randomised studies. P-683 admits full-length RCTs only.
candidate_explanations.quote: Non-randomized controlled study, conference abstracts, dissertations, cohort study, cross-sectional studies, case reports, protocols, review articles, and animal experimental studies.

candidate_explanations.difference: Evidence size and heterogeneity. P-680's aerobic estimate rests on 5 studies (df = 5) with I2 of about 89%. P-683's rests on 11 trials and 26 effect sizes in a multilevel model.
candidate_explanations.quote: The obtained Q value was 45.143 with a df= 5 and p < 0.001.

candidate_explanations.difference: Effect-size standardisation. Both use change scores, but P-683 imputes missing change SDs with r = 0.68, while P-680 standardises by change-score SD using study pre-post correlations (value not stated). Different assumed correlations change the SMD's scale.
candidate_explanations.quote: If the SD for change scores was not able to be calculated, it was estimated by using a correlation coefficient of 0.68

candidate_explanations.difference: Study quality. Excluding P-683's high risk-of-bias studies raises its AEwtM estimate from 0.48 to 0.6, narrowing but not closing the gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: After excluding studies with a high risk of bias, the effect sizes remained stable (Appendix L). However, there were some cases resulting in slightly higher effect sizes.

reason: Both reviews estimate the effect of aerobic exercise against control on cognition in MCI with change-score SMDs, and their estimates exclude each other: P-680 1.442 (0.624-2.260) against P-683 0.48 (0.18-0.79), with two-sample z of about 2.16. The comparison ignores the two trials, Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012, that sit in both strata. No figure under the other paper's condition reconciles them; P-683's quality-restricted 0.6 (0.28-0.93) still falls outside P-680's interval, though only by 0.024. The pair therefore qualifies as a magnitude discrepancy in the same direction. The candidate explanations (P-680's broader 'aerobic' class with music and dance trials, composite against global outcome, exclusion of amnestic trials, non-randomised designs, few heterogeneous studies, change-SD assumptions) are not shown by either paper to be sufficient. The record's own explanation, that P-680 pools a biomarker-reporting subset, is not supported by P-680's tables. The compared figures, however, are printed values, so condition 6 holds.

quotes.quote: The confidence interval for the difference in means varied from 0.642 to 2.260 (95 % CI). The Z-value obtained from the test of null hypothesis was 3.456 with p= 0.001.
pre-post correlation and standardized by score sd changes

AEwM had a large effect (k = 2, g = 1.2 [0.47, 1.94], while AEwtM demonstrated a low-to-moderate effect (k = 26, g = 0.48 [0.18, 0.79]), and dance had a moderate effect (k = 8, g = 0.55 [0.13, 0.96]).
standardized mean difference between change scores was calculated for all outcomes to account for the varying measures of cognitive function across studies
Six trials investigated the effects of dance (Chang et al., 2021; Doi et al., 2017; Kropacova et al., 2019; Lazarou et al., 2017; Qi et al., 2018; Zhu et al., 2020).
